address.q: ILO Digital Labour Platform Policy Tracker

analysis.analysis: A policy tracker is composed a phase ahead of itself. The record's limit (coverage still expanding; decisions planned) is the line the composition crosses, and its new instrument, the Convention, is one the record should carry once read from the ILO.
analysis.d: THE ILO DIGITAL LABOUR PLATFORM POLICY TRACKER, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a global policy database that monitors how countries regulate platform work through legislation, collective bargaining agreements, and judicial decisions.' Coverage ('more than 30 countries'), eight issues, its audience, and two related initiatives: the Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193) and the Observatory on AI and Work. Five cards, three of them the ILO's.
analysis.d_full: THE ILO DIGITAL LABOUR PLATFORM POLICY TRACKER, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a global policy database that monitors how countries regulate platform work through legislation, collective bargaining agreements, and judicial decisions.' Coverage ('more than 30 countries'), eight issues, its audience, and two related initiatives: the Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193) and the Observatory on AI and Work. Five cards, three of them the ILO's.
findings: THE TRACKER HELD. The eight issues (employment status, remuneration, algorithms, working time, data, safety, termination, collective bargaining) and the audience are the record's; the CBA component is its addition of 7 November 2025. Checked 2026-10-29 against the Labor Vector census record of the same day and the sources it saved.

JUDICIAL DECISIONS AHEAD OF THE TRACKER. The ILO's own page says 'the next phase of the project will focus on ... integrating judicial decisions related to the platform economy'; the composition gives them as tracked now.
'MORE THAN 30 COUNTRIES'. The record states no count; the figure is in no saved source.

THE CONVENTION. 'Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193)' rests on the ILO's digital labour platforms card; the record, compiled from the tracker's launch and expansion pages and the Observatory page, does not carry it. A record change to check against the ILO's own text.

read.notes: Claim boundary absent: the scope is inflated. The composition says it monitors regulation 'through legislation, collective bargaining agreements, and judicial decisions', but judicial decisions are the stated next phase, not yet integrated (census: 'NOT a court-decision database yet'); and 'Tracks policy developments, laws, and agreements across more than 30 countries' gives a count the records do not state (the application was not saved; the CBA component covers the European Union). Purpose present: 'support evidence-based policymaking' for governments and social partners is the launch page's 'facilitate social dialogue and evidence-based policymaking'. No date (14 August 2025; 7 November 2025). Deposit chain absent: the phased chain (launch, CBA component, planned judicial decisions) is not carried; the planned phase is composed as present. The Convention 'No. 193' of 2026 comes from card 3 (an ILO page) and lies outside the records; set beside the tracker, not merged. No inversion, no standing substitution.

measures.per_note: The ILO named; no person; no identifier; the ILO's own pages cited.
